sources.behaviour: every creature weenie of the world database, one row each, by weenie class: weenie.type 10 (WeenieType.Creature) and, from M6 item 16 E1e, weenie.type 15 (WeenieType.Cow), which ACE builds as a Creature subclass (Cow.cs:7; the other types it builds so, Vendor, GamePiece, Pet and CombatPet, are left out, each with why in tools/fight-sim/BestiaryRows.cs, AceIds.LeftOut). The rows are the server's own copy of ACE's open world database, loaded from the pinned world SQL (ACE-World-16PY-Patches v0.9.296, server/versions.json). Read through ACE's own models, queries only, and written by the generator: pwsh -File tools/fight-sim.ps1 bestiary (the columns are listed in tools/fight-sim/BestiaryTables.cs; bestiary --check writes the table again and compares it with this file). Written on 2026-11-17.

sources.computed: three values ACE computes are not stored; the reader (Session/Grounds/CreatureBehaviour.cs) computes them from this table's terms and the attributes creatures.json holds: maximum stamina is stamina_start + stamina_ranks + Endurance and maximum mana is mana_start + mana_ranks + Self, each never under 1 (ACE's CreatureVital.MaxValue, Entity/CreatureVital.cs:126-174, with the dats' vital formulas); the Run skill is run_start + run_ranks, plus Quickness when the skill is usable: trained, specialized, or untrained, the dats' skill table letting Run be used untrained (ACE's CreatureSkill.Current and IsUsable, Entity/CreatureSkill.cs:48-63 and 154-163). An attribute in these formulas is never under 1, an unstated one included (ACE's CreatureAttribute.Current, Entity/CreatureAttribute.cs:149-160). The hearing range of a row with -1 is its visual range. The three rates are vital points a heartbeat of the creature, and heartbeat_interval is the heartbeat's seconds (M6 item 16 E1e; ACE's 5 where the weenie states none, WorldObject_Tick.cs:47-48): a creature's heartbeat runs its vital tick (Creature_Tick.cs:14-49, Creature_Vitals.cs:81-95) and sets the next one that many seconds on (WorldObject_Tick.cs:98-108), so a rate over the interval is vital points a second, which the reader gives; with an interval of 0 or less ACE never beats (WorldObject_Tick.cs:56-68) and a vital never comes back.
sources.use: M6 item 16 E1d (docs/automation-engine.md section 2.1): the bestiary's record of a creature kind holds these beside what the automation reads today (the pinned awareness ranges, the ground profiles' pace and experience). The walker's creature feed reads the visual range beside the pinned one (E1f, --walk-awareness, default pinned); no other reader of the automation reads this table yet; the next slices move them one at a time.
